The fix adds a denylist of compromised certificates to the ssl module of Python. file-server-cleanup does not use TLS: it serves its metrics over plain HTTP, runs find to delete old files, and opens no other connections.
The vulnerable code is in infback9, in the contrib directory of zlib, which GDAL builds. The zlib library of Alpine does not include infback9: it exports no inflateBack9 function.

The advisory describes a path traversal in webpack-dev-middleware, a JavaScript package. zlib does not contain that code, and the image contains no webpack-dev-middleware.
The vulnerable code is in the Pod::Text module of perl, which formats POD documentation, for example for pod2text and perldoc. It needs a crafted POD document. No component formats POD documentation.

The vulnerable code is in gettext, which reads message catalogs from the directories in the LANGUAGE environment variable. To use it, an attacker needs to set LANGUAGE and a locale other than C or POSIX in the environment of a container, and to put a crafted catalog in it. The environment of each container comes from its pod spec. Only a user who can create or change pods sets it, and that user can already run any code in the container.

nccl-loopback runs only nvidia-smi and the nccl-tests binary, without a shell, and never runs Python. nccl-allreduce runs entrypoint.py, nvidia-smi, torchrun and the nccl_allreduce workers. gpu-health-monitor runs one Python process, which uses the DCGM library in remote or local-managed mode. dcgm-diag runs one Python process, which connects to a DCGM hostengine. syslog-health-monitor runs one Go binary, which links only libc and loads libsystemd to read the journal. A trace of the Python processes in each image records the Python modules and shared libraries that they load. ldd lists the libraries of the nccl-tests binary, NCCL and the CUDA runtime. ldd lists the libraries that the DCGM library and its modules link. zlib comes with the base image. The vulnerable code is in the gzip file functions, such as gzwrite(), gzprintf() and gzvprintf(). Where Python loads libz, it calls only the deflate, inflate and checksum functions, and none of the loaded libraries imports a gz* function. The nccl-loopback binaries do not load libz. The DCGM library and its modules do not link libz. The syslog-health-monitor binary and libsystemd do not link libz. zlib1g-dev holds headers and a static library that nothing links at run time.
